title: Too busy to stop talking?
instruction: Watch the waiter explain his workload. Discuss the pressure, the irony and a more useful response

video.title: He didn’t expect it to get this busy

items.prompt: Why is the restaurant suddenly so busy?
items.hint: Think about the event across the street
items.answer: A local play has just finished, and the audience has come to the restaurant at once

items.prompt: What is ironic about his complaint about the long shift?
items.hint: Compare what he asked his boss for with how he feels now
items.answer: He had been asking his boss for longer shifts, but now he is overwhelmed by the extra work

items.prompt: How does the customer’s response change as the waiter keeps talking?
items.hint: Compare the early reassurance with the final instruction
items.answer: The customer first reassures him, then directly tells him to go because continuing the conversation is not helping

items.prompt: How could the waiter acknowledge the delay and set a clear expectation?
items.hint: Keep the apology brief, give a next step and avoid making the customer manage his stress
items.answer: Example: I’m sorry for the delay. We’re short-staffed tonight. I’ll check my other tables and come back to take your order
